## 2026-11-17 02:02 · The builder to the lead (SR Leagues lane 2.157: a refusal that knows who is looking)

Builder 2.157 (lane/2.157-refusal), one technical question; I carry on with the rest meanwhile.

The line's "make a league's Page not found draw without scripts": in Next.js 16.4 any notFound()/forbidden() a page throws ends the server's render as an empty shell (record 020, line 15); I read the renderer (app-render.js, renderToStream's error recovery: an empty `<html id="__next_error__">`). Tried on this machine (next dev, stand-in):

1. A Suspense boundary around a refused page in [league]/layout: the server draws its fallback (so a refusal screen can be drawn without scripts), but the status becomes 200 (+ noindex). Status lost.
2. The proxy can set the status while the page draws normally: NextResponse.next({ status: 404, request: { headers } }) gave 404 with the page's heading drawn.
   So drawing AND keeping 403/404 needs both: the proxy works out the gate's answer for the address (resolveLeagueRequest + leaguePageOutcome, the same functions) to set the status, and the layout's Suspense fallback is the same refusal screen. Costs: a second session identification per league request (a Supabase round trip on real data) unless the proxy's answer is cached/passed on, and it covers only the gate's refusals (no access; hidden, binned or missing league). A page's own not-found (a hidden season, a missing team, another league's game) cannot be known in the proxy without its reads, so those stay blank without scripts.
   My plan unless you say otherwise: build everything else in the line now (words, ways on, other league's game -> 404, the account named now, the club admin's People, hidden = missing proof), and leave the scripts-off drawing as it is, reported with this evidence, since moving the gate into the proxy is a decision about record 020 that is yours. Say "proxy" if you want option 2+1 built in this lane.
